name: Dulverton Trust Conservation grants
summary: Grants to UK charities working on the health of UK wildlife habitat, mainly woodland and tree planting and management and coastal and marine protection. Applicants first take an eligibility quiz, then submit an expression of interest.

steps: Expression of Interest form, if eligible
Visit or online meeting, if taken forward

eligibility.rule: Be a UK registered charity or organisation with officially recognised charitable status
Income above £200,000, or a charity set up in the last 2 years
Have annual income of £10 million or less
Not primarily benefit residents of London or Northern Ireland
Not undertake animal welfare or projects concerning protection of single species
Not seek funding for capital projects, including property, land or vehicles

applicant_types.quote: We fund charities and CIOs with a national reach working within the above funding categories that meet our eligibility.

geography.quote: We support charities working on the health and resilience of the UK's wildlife habitat.

access.quote: To apply, complete our eligibility quiz (button below). If eligible, you will be provided with a link to our online Expression of Interest form.

effort.quote: The first step in applying is usually to fill out our eligibility quiz.
If you are eligible, you will be provided with a link to our Expression of Interest form.
we will conduct extensive desk-based research.
If we decide to take the application forward to the Sub-Committee, we will be in touch to arrange a visit or online meeting.

eligibility.quote: We do not offer funding to individuals, only UK registered charities and organisations with officially recognised charitable status.

The Trust will consider applications from newly established charities - by this, we mean charities established in the last two years, which do not yet have an income of £200,000, provided they meet the Trust&#39s other eligibility criteria.
We have an upper annual income threshold of £10 million and do not support charities with income above this.
We don't fund work primarily for the benefit of residents of London or Northern Ireland.
We do not at present fund animal welfare (including veterinary care) or projects concerning the protection of single species.
We do not currently fund capital projects, including the purchase of property, land or vehicles.

after_award.quote: We ask for a formal report when the funding has been expended (normally 12 months following each payment).
